summary: [MERGED into TKT-122] Inventory observes durable termination only after startupConverge — a deleted durable goes unnoticed for the length of the startup pass (TKT-127 ai-review)
description:
### Finding (TKT-127 adversarial ai-review, `gpt-5.6-sol`, 2026-07-27)

TKT-127 gave inventory the ADR-017 §236-241 termination guarantee access has had since TKT-97:
`Run` now calls `waitConsume(ctx, cc.Closed(), ...)`, so a deleted durable latches unready and
exits the process instead of stalling silently.

But it is observed **only after `startupConverge` returns**
(`services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go`, `Run`), and `startupConverge` can run long:
`reconcileAttempts = 3` passes, `retryBackoff = 5s` between them, and each pass makes a serial
catalog HTTP call per published pool. A durable deleted during that window is not noticed until
the pass finishes.

### What this is, and what it is not

Triaged **incidental** at TKT-127's review, deliberately — recording the reasoning so this ticket
does not get re-argued from scratch:

- It is **not a regression**. Before TKT-127 inventory never observed `cc.Closed()` at all; the
  same deletion left it up and reporting **ready** forever. TKT-127 strictly improves this.
- It is **not a false-ready lie**. `refreshStartupReadiness` stores `true` as the *last* statement
  of `startupConverge`, immediately before `waitConsume`. Throughout the reconciliation window
  readiness is `false`, which is honest. The ready-true-then-immediately-false window that follows
  is nanoseconds.
- What it **is**: a detection-latency gap. The process stays alive but unready, consuming nothing,
  for up to the length of the startup pass. Compose does not restart an unhealthy container
  (ADR-017 §236-238), so the process exit is the signal that matters, and it is late.

### Why it was not fixed in TKT-127

The obvious fix — race termination against `startupConverge` and cancel the pass on closure —
requires a goroutine and cancellation plumbing in a startup path that sits directly beside the
TKT-90 readiness serialization, inside a ticket whose stated constraint was "a refactor behind
existing tests". Worse, cancelling `startupConverge` via a derived context makes its returned
error indistinguishable from a shutdown cancellation, which would make **TKT-121** (inventory's
`main` does not filter cancellation-caused consumer errors) actively harder to fix.

So this needs a design decision, which means a plan gate. Hence a ticket.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A durable deleted while `startupConverge` is running is observed promptly, not after the pass.
- [ ] The termination error remains distinguishable from a shutdown cancellation at `main` — this
      must not regress TKT-121's premise.
- [ ] `refreshStartupReadiness` can never store `true` after the consume context has closed.
- [ ] A `Consumer.Run`-level test (not a direct `waitConsume` call) with reconciliation blocked and
      the consume context closing: asserts prompt return, the exact diagnostic, and that readiness
      never becomes true. The TKT-127 tests call `waitConsume` directly and cannot catch this.
- [ ] TKT-90's serialization guarantee still holds; its tests still pass unmodified.
- [ ] `make check` green.

**Consider taking TKT-121 with it** — the two meet at the same error channel and the fixes interact.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Raised by the **TKT-127 adversarial ai-review** (`gpt-5.6-sol`), which returned
`verdict: needs-attention` on exactly this point and recommended racing termination against the
startup pass.

Triaged **incidental** rather than blocking at TKT-127, per `quality-practices.md` §2: it is real,
but it is not a defect *in that diff* — it is a residual gap in a guarantee that diff created,
and the pre-existing behaviour was strictly worse. Fixing it properly is a concurrency change to a
startup path with a live interaction with TKT-121, which earns its own plan gate.

The reviewer's other point is worth carrying over verbatim: *"The new tests invoke `waitConsume`
directly and therefore pass despite this production ordering defect."* That is correct, and it is
why the COS above requires a `Run`-level test rather than another helper-level one.

Related: TKT-121 (inventory `main`'s cancellation race — likely wants doing together), ADR-034
(§Consequences names this gap explicitly), TKT-123 (the diagnostic cannot distinguish causes).

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 validation — re-verified against HEAD `ac2952b`

**Still real.** `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:503` runs `startupConverge` before `waitConsume` at :524; the residual is documented in the code comment at :515-517. Its stated companion TKT-121 is now **Done**, which removes the "makes TKT-121 harder" objection — and TKT-122 now covers the same error channel in access. Sequence 122/135 together.

**Verdict: still worth doing → Ready.** Not DoR-baked: the 8-item shaping happens when the ticket is claimed, per the owner's drain-the-debt call.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Merged into TKT-122 — do not claim

This ticket's scope now lives in **TKT-122** (Consumer termination lifecycle, access + inventory: shutdown-time drain and startup-window detection), which carries it verbatim under an *Absorbed TKT-135* section. Moved out of Ready so it cannot be picked up in parallel. Nothing was dropped — reopen this only if the merge is reversed at plan time.
